canonical_statement: Let $t\geq 1$ and let $d_t$ be the density of the set of integers $n\in\mathbb{N}$ for which $t$ can be represented as the sum of distinct divisors of $n$.Do there exist constants $c_1,c_2>0$ such that\[d_t \sim \frac{c_1}{(\log t)^{c_2}}\]as $t\to \infty$?

must_determine: A complete proof of the affirmative proposition over its full stated scope.
If the proposition is existential, an explicit witness/construction or a rigorous existence proof, together with verification of every required property.
If the proposition is universal, coverage of every allowed object/parameter rather than sampled instances or a restricted family.
All endpoint, degeneracy, distinctness, integrality, normalization, and full-sequence conditions required by the canonical statement.

Reviewer-mandated close condition: close_branch_A: must_determine does not explicitly require proving existence of the natural density d_t for every t ≥ 1 as part of the affirmative close; since the canonical statement presupposes d_t ('let d_t be the density'), a close that only proves the asymptotic for some a-priori density-like quantity would be a non-result. Add an explicit obligation: for every t ≥ 1 the set has a natural density, and the asymptotic d_t ~ c₁/(log t)^{c₂} holds with c₁, c₂ > 0 independent of t.
close_branch_A.statement: AFFIRMATIVE CLOSE: prove the canonical proposition exactly as stated, with every quantifier, domain restriction, asymptotic qualifier, and structural condition preserved.

must_determine: A concrete counterexample/parameter choice satisfying every premise but violating the asserted conclusion, or an equivalent proof of the exact negation.
The quantifiers reversed exactly according to classical logic, including “for all sufficiently large”, “infinitely many”, “for every ε”, and nested existential/universal binders.
Verification that the negative witness uses the same domains, normalizations, and definitions as the affirmative statement.
No appeal to a weakened/strawman version of the target.
close_branch_B.statement: NEGATIVE CLOSE: prove the literal logical negation of the canonical proposition—not failure of a proof strategy, not a counterexample to a stronger variant, and not a refutation of an informal guess.

definitions: Formal-semantics guard: any Lean or equivalent formalization used in the campaign must be semantically bound back to this canonical statement. Types, endpoint conventions, and degenerate cases may not be guessed; any formal/prose mismatch must be resolved explicitly before claiming closure.
Quantifier-order guard: the quantifiers occur in the order stated and may not be commuted, weakened, or replaced by sampled cases. Salient source phrases include: there exist constants $c_1.

Integer-domain guard: preserve exactly whether variables range over positive integers, all naturals, or integers. If a formalization uses `ℕ` (and hence contains 0) while the prose uses positive integers, the 0/1 endpoint cases must be proved equivalent or handled separately; they may not be silently discarded.
Integrality is load-bearing wherever the statement specifies integers; real/continuous relaxations do not inherit the claim without an exact transfer theorem.

Limit guard: every lim/limsup/liminf statement is along the full directed sequence specified by the source (normally the natural variable tending to infinity), not merely along a favorable subsequence. A finite limit is distinct from divergence to infinity and from bounded limsup.

Asymptotic-notation guard: `~`, `o`, `O`, `≪`, and `≫` keep their standard distinct meanings. Any hidden constant may depend only on parameters explicitly shown as subscripts/fixed before the limiting variable, never on the limiting variable itself.

Density guard: natural density, upper density, lower density, logarithmic density, positive density, and "almost all" are different notions. Use exactly the density notion named in the statement and preserve whether existence of the density itself is part of the claim.

Divisibility guard: divisors, proper/unitary divisors, multiplicities, gcd/coprimality, and strict divisibility inequalities are interpreted exactly as stated; empty/zero edge cases require explicit treatment.

Distinctness guard: every distinctness/pairwise condition is structural, not cosmetic; multisets, repeated witnesses, or quotienting by symmetry may be used only when they preserve the original distinct objects exactly.

Review-authority rule for this repaired contract: the immutable canonical_statement is the controlling mathematical target. Where a reviewer defect identifies an exact source/Lean encoding as the intended convention, that exact encoding is binding; any alternative convention mentioned only to expose ambiguity is forbidden unless exact equivalence to the controlling target is proved.

Binding semantic repair: definitions: the density notion is never defined. The canonical statement says 'let d_t be the density' but the contract never pins that this is the natural density d_t = lim_{x→∞} |{n ≤ x : n ∈ DivisorSumSet t}|/x, nor that existence of this limit for every t ≥ 1 is itself part of the affirmative claim. The Lean formalization makes it explicit (∀ t > 0, (DivisorSumSet t).HasDensity (d t)); a reformulation could silently substitute upper/lower density or drop the existence obligation. The generic 'Density guard' sentence lists notions but does not bind THIS statement to natural density with existence included.

Binding semantic repair: definitions: domain/endpoint mismatch unresolved. The prose restricts to t ≥ 1 while the Lean formalization quantifies over all t > 0 (and DivisorSumSet 0 = univ, density 1, which is consistent but must be reconciled). The 'Integer-domain guard' mentions this generically but the contract never states which convention is canonical for the close, nor that t = 0 (empty sum) and t = 1 (divisor 1 only, density 1) degenerate cases are handled.

Binding semantic repair: definitions: log base is unpinned. c₁ absorbs the base change only if c₂ is fixed; the contract must state natural log (as in Real.log) so that the pair (c₁, c₂) is well-defined and the asymptotic is base-invariant in the intended way.

Binding semantic repair: definitions: the ranges of c₁ and c₂ are not pinned as positive reals (vs positive integers/reals); the Lean source requires c₁ > 0, c₂ > 0 : ℝ. Also whether c₁, c₂ may depend on nothing (absolute constants) versus being allowed to be non-unique/non-canonical (multiple pairs may work) should be stated: the claim is pure existence, not uniqueness.

Binding semantic repair: definitions: the representation convention 'sum of distinct divisors of n' is not pinned: divisors are positive divisors of n, each usable at most once, empty sum allowed only for t = 0, and the set DivisorSumSet t is {n : ∃ s ⊆ divisors n, t = ∑ i ∈ s, i}. The Distinctness guard is generic; the contract should bind the exact Lean predicate (∃ s ⊆ Nat.divisors n, t = ∑ i ∈ s, i) to the prose.

Add an explicit obligation: for every t ≥ 1 the set has a natural density, and the asymptotic d_t ~ c₁/(log t)^{c₂} holds with c₁, c₂ > 0 independent of t.
invariants_that_must_survive_every_refor: The canonical statement text is immutable; every proof target must imply exactly that statement (or its literal negation for a negative close).
Every quantifier, domain, hypothesis, strict/non-strict inequality, endpoint, normalization, and parameter dependency survives every reformulation.
Discrete structure is preserved: integrality, distinctness, ordering, multiplicity/set-vs-multiset conventions, and exact cardinalities may not be relaxed silently.
Any asymptotic/eventual claim retains the same limiting variable and full-sequence requirement.
The exact density notion named by the statement, including existence versus upper/lower density and positivity/zero requirements.
All stated distinctness/pairwise conditions and the exact handling of trivial coincidences.
known_traps: QUANTIFIER SLIP: exchanging ∀ and ∃, moving an epsilon/constant after the limiting variable, or replacing “all sufficiently large” by “infinitely many”.
SAMPLED-TO-UNIVERSAL: checking many finite instances and promoting the observation to an unrestricted theorem without a valid finite-reduction theorem.
DOMAIN DRIFT: proving a translated/scaled/relaxed version without an exact map back to the original domain, endpoints, and discrete constraints.
STRENGTH CONFUSION: refuting a stronger folklore conjecture does not refute the canonical claim; proving a weaker statement does not prove it.
ASYMPTOTIC CONSTANT DRIFT: hidden constants cannot depend on the main variable, and one-sided O/Ω bounds do not establish Θ/asymptotic equivalence.
DENSITY SUBSTITUTION: upper, lower, natural, logarithmic, Banach, and almost-sure/density-one notions are not interchangeable.
DISTINCTNESS LOSS: a witness with repeated elements or a multiset solution is invalid when the source requires distinct elements/representations.

Explicit problem-specific trap: known_traps: missing trap — 'presupposed-object trap': treating d_t as given/defined rather than proving its existence; the statement's phrasing 'let d_t be the density' hides an existence obligation that a reformulation could silently drop.

Explicit problem-specific trap: known_traps: missing trap — constant-pair non-uniqueness: the claim is ∃ c₁ ∃ c₂; a proof producing one valid pair suffices, but a reformulation demanding a canonical/unique pair, or one proving the statement for a specific guessed (c₁, c₂) without proving the asymptotic, corrupts the close.
non_results: A theorem for only a selected finite set of parameter values when the statement is uniform or asymptotic.
A result only on a favorable subsequence, density-one subset, almost-everywhere set, or “generic” family when the canonical statement requires the full sequence/all objects.
A numerical fit, heuristic, Monte Carlo result, floating-point experiment, or finite computation without a proved finite-reduction/transfer theorem to the canonical claim.
A restricted-family result obtained by adding hypotheses not present in the statement, unless those hypotheses are proved without loss of generality for every canonical instance.
A conditional theorem whose decisive premise is an unproved conjecture of comparable strength.
A reduction to an equivalent-strength open problem, a tautological rephrasing, or a definition of the requested answer in terms of the original unresolved predicate.
A continuous/real-valued/LP/SDP relaxation without a proved integrality or exact-transfer theorem when the canonical objects are discrete.
A stronger-looking statement in a different normalization/domain that does not formally imply the canonical statement.
A one-sided asymptotic estimate when the target asks for an equality, equivalence, limit, or two-sided order.
A bound with a constant depending on the limiting variable or on hidden arithmetic data of that variable.
Replacing liminf by limsup, a full limit by a limsup/liminf statement, or divergence by unboundedness on a sparse subsequence.
Positive upper density in place of positive lower/natural density; existence of a limsup in place of existence of the named density; or any other substitution among non-equivalent density notions.

Explicit non-result: non_results: missing problem-specific near-miss: proving only the Erdős two-sided power-of-log bounds (1/log^c₃ < d_t < 1/log^c₄, the solved variant in the source) is NOT a close of the asymptotic-equivalence question; the contract's non_results list one-sided estimates generically but should name this exact solved-variant trap since it is the most tempting substitute here.

Explicit non-result: non_results: missing near-miss: proving the asymptotic only for a subsequence of t, or proving limsup/liminf of d_t·(log t)^{c₂} are positive and finite in place of an actual limit/equivalence, or fixing c₂ = 1 (or any specific exponent) without proving the existence claim as stated.
permitted_background: Definitions and elementary facts in the named mathematical domain, with every imported theorem used only under its exact published/formal hypotheses.

Standard algebraic, combinatorial, analytic, probabilistic, number-theoretic, set-theoretic, and asymptotic lemmas needed to manipulate the objects appearing in the statement; no theorem equivalent in strength to the target may be assumed.

Exact finite computation, SAT/SMT/MILP, interval arithmetic, symbolic algebra, exhaustive enumeration, or custom verified tooling may be used as a lemma/certificate when its finite search space and transfer to the unrestricted claim are proved.
Lean/Mathlib or another proof assistant may certify intermediate and final results; kernel acceptance does not by itself excuse a semantic mismatch with the canonical statement.
Standard proved facts about primes, divisibility, congruences, multiplicative/additive functions, and elementary/analytic number theory may be used with explicit dependency and range conditions.
Standard real/measure/asymptotic analysis may be used, but pointwise, uniform, almost-everywhere, in-measure, density, limsup, and full-limit conclusions may not be interchanged.
